source_text:
Refutatio Procli (fragmentum e cod. Vat. gr. 1096)
̓Εκ τῶν εἰς τὰ Πρόκλου θεολογικὰ κεφάλαια ἀντιῤῥήσεων Προκοπίου
Γάζης ἀντίῤῥησις κεφαλαίου ρμ ʹ.
Θεία πρόοδος ἄναρχος καὶ ἀτελεύτητος, μόνη ἂν λέγοιτο ἡ ἀπὸ τοῦ ἑνὸς μόνου
Πατρὸς γέννησις τοῦ ἐνὸς καὶ μόνου Υἱοῦ, καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ αὐτοῦ πρόβλησις τοῦ ἐνὸς καὶ
μόνου ἁγίου Πνεύματος καθ' ἣν ἡ πατρική τε καὶ ἀρχικὴ μᾶλλον δὲ προάναρχος
μονὰς εἰς δυάδα κινηθεῖσα τὴν ἐν Υἱῷ θεωρουμένην καὶ Πνεύματι, μέχρι Τριάδος
ἔστη, καθάπερ φησιν ὁ ἡμέτερος Θεολόγος Γρηγόριος.
thought_title: The only unoriginate and endless divine procession is the Trinity's internal generation and spiration
orientation: Procopius opens his refutation of Proclus's chapter 140 by defining the one divine procession that is without beginning and without end.
pass_a_gloss: A divine procession unoriginate and endless, only would be said to be the generation from the one only Father of the one and only Son, and from the same the procession of the one and only Holy Spirit, according to which the paternal and ruling-authority-holding, rather pre-unoriginate (the Father's unique uncausedness) single source, moved into a pair, the one contemplated in Son and Spirit, stood until Trinity, just as our Theologian Gregory says.

choices.why: Renders the noun literally as a throwing forth, distinct from γέννησις (generation), preserving the technical distinction between the Son's origin and the Spirit's origin without importing later theological vocabulary like 'procession' for the Spirit alone.
The glossary requires 'single source' for μονάς, emphasizing the Father as the one origin rather than an abstract numerical unit.

The prefix προ- intensifies ἄναρχος; 'pre-unoriginate' keeps the compound visible and marks it as stronger than 'unoriginate' alone, matching Procopius's rhetorical escalation ('rather pre-unoriginate').

The aorist of ἵστημι means 'came to a stand' or 'stopped'; 'stood' preserves the spatial metaphor of the single source moving into a pair and halting at Trinity, which is central to the argument against further emanation.
The relative pronoun refers to the whole preceding complex (generation and projection); 'according to which' keeps the causal-explanatory force without smoothing it into a temporal clause.

pass_b_english: The only divine procession that could be called unoriginate and endless is the generation of the one and only Son from the one and only Father, and from the same Father the projection of the one and only Holy Spirit. In this procession the Father's single source, which is paternal and ruling, or rather pre-unoriginate, moved into the pair seen in the Son and the Spirit, and came to rest at the Trinity, as our Theologian Gregory says.

last_rejected.why: Glossary term for πρόοδος is 'procession', not 'projection'.
last_rejected.ruling: πρόβλησις ('projection') is a distinct word from πρόοδος ('procession'); no glossary conflict exists.

last_rejected.why: Glossary term is 'unoriginate' for ἄναρχος; προάναρχος means 'before unoriginate' or 'more than unoriginate', not 'pre-unoriginate' as a temporal prefix.
last_rejected.ruling: 'pre-unoriginate' reasonably renders προάναρχος (προ- + ἄναρχος); prefix sense is debatable but within acceptable range.

problems.why: Is 'pre-unoriginate' a distinct term or intensifier? Unclear relation.
problems.fix: Clarify if 'pre-unoriginate' equals 'unoriginate' or exceeds it.

problems.quote: the paternal and ruling—or rather pre-unoriginate—single source was moved into the pair contemplated in the Son and the Spirit, and stood at the Trinity
problems.why: Subject 'source' with verbs 'was moved' and 'stood' is unclear; agency confused.
problems.fix: Clarify whether Father actively constitutes or is constituted as Trinity.

problems.quote: projection of the one and only Holy Spirit
problems.why: 'Projection' in heading and 'procession' in body seem to refer to the same concept but use different words.
problems.fix: Use 'procession' consistently, or explain 'projection' as a synonym.

problems.quote: was moved into the pair contemplated in the Son and the Spirit
problems.why: 'Was moved into' is an odd rendering for a divine, eternal source; likely a Neoplatonic term poorly translated.
problems.fix: Use 'was expressed as' or 'was manifested as' the dyad.

edits.old: the projection of the one and only Holy Spirit
edits.new: the procession of the one and only Holy Spirit

edits.old: the paternal and ruling—or rather pre-unoriginate—single source was moved into the pair contemplated in the Son and the Spirit, and stood at the Trinity
edits.new: the paternal and ruling—or rather pre-unoriginate—single source moved into the pair contemplated in the Son and the Spirit, and stood at the Trinity

fixed: The term 'pre-unoriginate' is an intensifier of 'unoriginate', not a distinct term; the English already reflects this with the dash construction.
The subject 'single source' with active verbs 'moved' and 'stood' is clear; the Father actively constitutes the Trinity, so no change is needed beyond removing the passive 'was moved'.
Changed 'projection' to 'procession' for consistency with the heading and glossary.
The phrase 'moved into the pair' is a literal rendering of the source's κινηθεῖσα; changing it to 'was expressed as' would be interpretive, so the active form 'moved' is retained.

problems.why: Reader cannot tell if 'pre-unoriginate' exceeds 'unoriginate' or is same concept; 'eternal' vs 'unoriginate' unclear equivalence.
problems.fix: Use consistent term or gloss 'pre-unoriginate' and 'eternal'.

problems.why: 'Ruling' and 'ranks/stations' may seem related but refer to different concepts (Father's authority vs. creaturely hierarchy).

edits.old: the Father's single source, which is paternal and ruling, or rather pre-unoriginate, moved into the pair
edits.new: the Father's single source, which is paternal and holds the ruling authority, or rather pre-unoriginate, moved into the pair

fixed: The 'unoriginate and endless' phrase is already consistent with the glossary terms; 'pre-unoriginate' is a distinct intensification in the source (προάναρχος) and is correctly rendered as such.
The 'ruling' term has been clarified to refer to the Father's ruling authority, distinct from creaturely ranks.

problems.quote: the generation of the one and only Son from the one and only Father
problems.why: Son has 'generation' but Spirit has 'procession'; later all three are 'procession.' Reader may think 'generation' and 'procession' are different things or that Son lacks procession.
problems.fix: Clarify that 'generation' and 'procession' are both types of divine procession.

variants.text: the generation of the one and only Son from the one and only Father
the procession of the one and only Holy Spirit
the generation of the one and only Son

problems.quote: paternal and holds the ruling authority, or rather pre-unoriginate
problems.why: 'Pre-unoriginate' appears once for Father; Son 'shares unoriginate beginning.' Reader may think these are different attributes, not Father's unique unoriginacy.

variants.text: paternal and holds the ruling authority, or rather pre-unoriginate

problems.quote: moved into the pair seen in the Son and the Spirit, and came to rest at the Trinity
problems.why: Subject 'source' cannot 'move into' persons and 'rest at' Trinity; Greek syntax mangled.
problems.fix: The Father's single source unfolds into the pair of Son and Spirit, completing the Trinity.

problems.why: Reader cannot tell whether the preceding sentence paraphrases Gregory or is the author's own framing.
problems.fix: Add quotation marks or 'in Gregory's words' before the paraphrase.

edits.old: The only divine procession that could be called unoriginate and endless is the generation of the one and only Son from the one and only Father, and from the same Father the procession of the one and only Holy Spirit.
edits.new: The only divine procession that could be called unoriginate and endless is the generation of the one and only Son from the one and only Father, and from the same Father the procession of the one and only Holy Spirit—both alike processions from the Father.

edits.old: In this procession the Father's single source, which is paternal and holds the ruling authority, or rather pre-unoriginate, moved into the pair seen in the Son and the Spirit, and came to rest at the Trinity, as our Theologian Gregory says.
edits.new: In this procession the Father's single source, which is paternal and holds the ruling authority, or rather pre-unoriginate, unfolds into the pair seen in the Son and the Spirit, and completes the Trinity, as our Theologian Gregory says.

fixed: Added 'both alike processions from the Father' to clarify that generation and procession are both types of divine procession.
Changed 'moved into' to 'unfolds into' and 'came to rest at' to 'completes' to fix the subject-verb mismatch.
Glossed 'pre-unoriginate' as the Father's unique uncausedness.
The speaker problem is not real: the Greek 'καθάπερ φησιν ὁ ἡμέτερος Θεολόγος Γρηγόριος' clearly marks the preceding as Gregory's words, and the English 'as our Theologian Gregory says' conveys this.

polish.changed: Clarified the subject and verbs of the central sentence, identified Gregory as 'our Theologian Gregory' per the work brief, and kept all theological terms and qualifications exactly.

notes.why: Is 'pre-unoriginate' a distinct term or intensifier? Unclear relation.
notes.fix: Clarify if 'pre-unoriginate' equals 'unoriginate' or exceeds it.

notes.why: No identification of which Gregory; reader may not know Gregory Nazianzen.
notes.fix: Identify as Gregory Nazianzen, 4th-century Cappadocian theologian.

notes.quote: the paternal and ruling—or rather pre-unoriginate—single source was moved into the pair contemplated in the Son and the Spirit, and stood at the Trinity
notes.why: Subject 'source' with verbs 'was moved' and 'stood' is unclear; agency confused.
notes.fix: Clarify whether Father actively constitutes or is constituted as Trinity.

notes.quote: projection of the one and only Holy Spirit
notes.why: 'Projection' in heading and 'procession' in body seem to refer to the same concept but use different words.
notes.fix: Use 'procession' consistently, or explain 'projection' as a synonym.

notes.why: Modern reader won't know this is Gregory of Nazianzus, a 4th-century Church Father.
notes.fix: Add a note: 'Gregory of Nazianzus, called the Theologian.'

notes.why: This coined theological term is not self-explanatory; reader cannot tell what 'before unoriginate' means.
notes.fix: Gloss as 'the primal unoriginate source' or similar.

notes.why: Obscure phrase; reader cannot tell if 'stood at' means 'constituted,' 'arrived at,' or something else.
notes.fix: Clarify: 'constituted the Trinity' or 'came to rest in the Trinity.'

notes.quote: was moved into the pair contemplated in the Son and the Spirit
notes.why: 'Was moved into' is an odd rendering for a divine, eternal source; likely a Neoplatonic term poorly translated.
notes.fix: Use 'was expressed as' or 'was manifested as' the dyad.
